name: Carrion Defense Works Bone Saw BS-3 'Butcher'
description: A forearm-mounted reciprocating blade designed for breaching body armor and cyberware housings in close-quarters combat. The BS-3 extends a 20cm carbide-toothed blade from a housing strapped to the user's forearm, oscillating at 4,000 strokes per minute with enough force to cut through Grade 3 composite armor in under two seconds. Carrion designed it as a field tool for emergency cyberware removal and armor breach, but its adoption by close-combat specialists has given it a reputation as the most visceral weapon in the corporate arsenal. The sound it makes cutting through metal is reportedly indistinguishable from the sound it makes cutting through bone.
legality: Licensed — field engineering and emergency services
specifications:
blade length: 20 cm reciprocating carbide
oscillation rate: 4,000 strokes per minute
armor breach time: Grade 3 composite in 1.8 seconds
power source: Forearm-mounted lithium cell, 15 minutes continuous
weight: 1.1 kg total assembly
mount: Forearm strap with wrist trigger
blade replacement: Tool-free swap, Φ80 per blade
story_hooks: A rash of cyberware thefts in the mid-tiers involves victims whose implant housings were cut open with surgical precision using BS-3 blade patterns — the thieves are harvesting augmentations from living people.

Carrion has released an updated blade material that cuts through their competitors' armor significantly faster than their own — raising questions about whether the blade was designed as a product or a strategic weapon against rival equipment.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutal industrial apparatus—a compact reciprocating saw mechanism housed in a reinforced polymer casing, mounted horizontally along the forearm like a prosthetic limb. The blade extends forward in a predatory stance, evoking surgical precision corrupted by violence.
physical_description.dimensions: Housing: 18cm long × 6cm wide × 4cm tall. Blade extension: 20cm reciprocating stroke. Total forearm assembly fits standard adult arm circumference 20-28cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced—1.1kg distributed across the forearm creates a weighted sensation without dragging. Feels anchored to the arm, not alien.
physical_description.primary_material: Titanium-reinforced polymer casing with steel internal gearing. Carbide blade segments mounted in hardened steel carrier.
physical_description.finish: Industrial matte gunmetal gray with aggressive heat-scored black sections along the blade housing. Carbide teeth gleam dull silver against darker steel backing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with midnight black accent panels. Carbide blade picks up light with a pale, almost bone-white shimmer.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized impact-polymer forearm strap with deep grooves. Wrist trigger mechanism is knurled steel with tension-resistant silicone pad.
distinctive_features: Four carbide sawtooth segments visible in the blade carrier, each beveled at aggressive angle
Ventilation slits along housing for heat dissipation—arranged in downward-pointing chevrons
Lithium cell indicator: three-point LED status light embedded in the wrist trigger guard (red/amber/green)
Blade assembly marked with tool-free quick-swap grooves
Speed governor dial on the upper housing (three positions: precision/standard/breach)
Faint scorch marks and micro-scratches across the casing from extended use
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CARRION DEFENSE WORKS stamped in clean sans-serif on the wrist trigger guard. Serial plate mounted on the inner forearm strap, low-visibility matte aluminum. Small carbide replacement symbol etched near the blade housing.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but visibly used—minor scoring on the polymer housing, carbide blade edges sharp but showing micro-fractures from repeated cutting. Heat discoloration around ventilation slits. The kind of wear that suggests field deployment and proper maintenance.
